Ainamuuren.saveDetails: +1 de bonificador de estado a las salvaciones contra conjuros y efectos sagrados

action->Blackfrost Evasion.name: Evasión de escarcha negra
action->Blackfrost Evasion.description:
Desencadenante Ainamuuren recibe al menos 35 de daño físico de un solo ataque y no está actualmente desencorporado

Efecto Ainamuuren se desencorpora en una ventisca arremolinada de escarcha negra durante 3 asaltos. Durante este tiempo, obtiene resistencia 10 al daño físico y debilidad 10 al daño de fuerza. Obtiene una Velocidad de vuelo de 40 pies, pero la única acción que puede realizar es Volar. Mientras está desencorporado, la primera vez cada asalto que Ainamuuren entra en el espacio de otra criatura o una criatura entra en el espacio de Ainamuuren, esa criatura recibe @Damage[4d8[cold]] y queda expuesta a la escarcha negra. Al comienzo de su turno, Ainamuuren puede terminar este efecto como acción gratuita.

action->Reactive Strike (Tentacle Only).name:
<Compendium> la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.W7SbTykXrNwxDzJc]
Golpe reactivo (solo tentáculo)

action->Reactive Tentacles.name: Tentáculos reactivos
action->Reactive Tentacles.description: Al comienzo de su turno, cuando Ainamuuren recupera sus acciones, obtiene una reaccion adicional que solo puede usar para realizar un Ataque de oportunidad.

action->Dreams of the Blackfrost Whale.name: Sueños de la Ballena de Escarcha Negra
action->Dreams of the Blackfrost Whale.description:
Frecuencia una vez al día

Efecto Ainamuuren fija su mirada de muchos ojos en un único objetivo que pueda ver a 60 pies o menos, y después abre sus fauces para liberar un torrente de susurros canalizados desde la mente dormida de Osoyo. La criatura objetivo debe intentar una salvación de @Check[will|dc:32].

Éxito crítico La criatura no se ve afectada.

Éxito La criatura soporta un breve instante en el que cree estar prisionera en el hielo, como Osoyo durante miles de años, y queda @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Lentificada 1} durante 1 asalto.

Fallo La visión de estar prisionera en el hielo es más profunda; en unos pocos segundos, la criatura soporta lo que parecen mil años de cautiverio. La criatura queda @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralizada} hasta el final de su siguiente turno, tras lo cual sale de la parálisis @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Anonadada 1}.

Fallo crítico Como fallo, pero la criatura no se recupera automáticamente de la parálisis al final de su turno. En su lugar, puede intentar una nueva salvación CD 32. Con un éxito, la parálisis termina y queda anonadada 1; con un fallo, la parálisis continúa otro asalto.

action->Invasive Blackfrost.name:
<Compendium> la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-family-ability-glossary.Item.kLQ0eq18SvKEvggc]
Escarcha negra invasiva
action->Invasive Blackfrost.description:
la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-family-ability-glossary.Item.kLQ0eq18SvKEvggc]

Los personajes caminantes de puertas no son inmunes a los efectos de escarcha negra infligidos por Ainamuuren.

Esta aflicción no puede reducirse por debajo de la etapa 1, ni puede curarse el daño que causa, hasta que sea tratada con éxito mediante @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.SUKaxVZW2TlM8lu0]{Purificar aflicción} o un efecto similar; después, la aflicción puede eliminarse como una enfermedad normal. Una criatura que muere por daño de frío mientras está maldita con escarcha negra se alza como muerto de escarcha negra tras 24 horas. La escarcha negra tiene rango de contrarrestar 10.

Salvación @Check[fortitude|dc:32]

Etapa 1 @Damage[4d6[cold]] (1 minuto)

Etapa 2 debilidad al frío 5 y @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drenado 1} (1 día)

Etapa 3 debilidad al frío 10 y @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drenado 2} (1 día)

action->Twist Deviance.name: Retorcer desviación
action->Twist Deviance.description:
Ainamuuren alarga la mano, cierra los dedos en un puño y retuerce el brazo como si estuviera tirando y desgarrando. En el mismo instante, todos los caminantes de puertas en un @Template[cone|distance:60] que Ainamuuren pueda ver sienten cómo las señales que llevan en el cuerpo desde que salieron de su pico del Momento Perdido arden de dolor, como si Ainamuuren hubiera @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Agarrado} esa carne y la estuviera retorciendo y rasgando. Los objetivos deben intentar una salvación de @Check[will|dc:32]. Ainamuuren no puede usar Retorcer desviación de nuevo durante [[/br 1d4 #Recarga Retorcer desviación]]{1d4 asaltos}.

Éxito crítico La criatura no se ve afectada.

Éxito La criatura soporta un breve instante de dolor horrible y recibe @Damage[4d8[mental]].

Fallo El dolor es mucho mayor, y por un momento la criatura queda convencida de que la parte de su carne adornada con la señal del caminante de puertas ha sido arrancada. Recibe @Damage[8d8[mental]] y no puede usar sus aptitudes desviantes durante 1 asalto.

Fallo crítico Como fallo, pero recibe @Damage[16d8[mental]] y no puede usar sus aptitudes desviantes durante 1 minuto.

Alkoasha.name: Alkoasha
Alkoasha.publicNotes: Hydras son multiheaded, foul-tempered serpentine beasts con voracious appetites, widely feared for su regeneration abilities.

action->Hydra Regeneration.name: Regeneración de hidra
action->Hydra Regeneration.description:
La hidra tiene regeneración igual a 3 × el número de cabezas que posee. Si al cuerpo de una hidra le falta alguna cabeza y los muñones restantes no han sido cauterizados, la hidra intenta una salvación de @Check[fortitude|immutable:true|dc:25] después de recuperar Puntos de Golpe por regeneración. Con un éxito, un muñón sin cauterizar vuelve a hacer crecer una cabeza; con un éxito crítico, vuelven a crecer dos muñones sin cauterizar. La regeneración de la hidra solo se desactiva por completo si todas sus cabezas son cercenadas y todos los muñones son cauterizados, momento en el que muere.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.Regeneración]

action->Alkoasha's Head Regrowth.name: Recrecimiento de cabezas de Alkoasha
action->Alkoasha's Head Regrowth.description:
Alkoasha tiene diez cabezas. Una criatura puede intentar cercenar una de las cabezas de la hidra apuntando específicamente a ella e infligiéndole daño igual a los Puntos de Golpe de la cabeza. Una cabeza que no sea cercenada por completo recupera todos sus Puntos de Golpe al final del turno de cualquier criatura.

Alkoasha puede regenerar una cabeza cercenada mediante Regeneración de hidra. Una criatura puede impedir este recrecimiento infligiendo daño de ácido o fuego al muñón y cauterizándolo. Los efectos de ácido o fuego contra un solo objetivo deben apuntar a un muñón específico, pero los efectos que infligen daño de salpicadura o afectan áreas que cubren todo el espacio de la hidra cauterizan todos los muñones si infligen daño de ácido o fuego. Si el ataque que cercena una cabeza inflige cualquier daño de ácido o fuego, el muñón queda cauterizado al instante. Si las diez cabezas quedan cauterizadas, la hidra muere.

Cabeza de hidra

  • Puntos de Golpe 15
  • Inmunidades daño de área
  • Debilidades cortante 5

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.uZJOdounIHaFDC1t]{Efecto: Cabezas de hidra}

action->Multiple Opportunities.name: Múltiples oportunidades
action->Multiple Opportunities.description: Una hidra obtiene una reacción adicional por asalto por cada cabeza que tenga más allá de la primera, que solo puede usar para realizar Ataques de Oportunidad. No puede usar más de 1 reacción ante la misma acción desencadenante, incluso si una criatura abandona varias casillas dentro de su alcance, y la hidra debe usar una cabeza distinta para cada Ataque de Oportunidad que realice. Siempre que una de las cabezas de la hidra sea cercenada, la hidra pierde 1 de sus reacciones adicionales por asalto.

action->Focused Assault.name: Asalto concentrado
action->Focused Assault.description: La hidra ataca a un único objetivo con sus cabezas, abrumando a su enemigo con múltiples ataques y dejándole muy poco espacio para esquivar. La hidra realiza Golpes con sus colmillos. Con un ataque éxitoso, la hidra inflige al objetivo el daño de su Golpe de colmillos, más [[/r 1d6]] de daño adicional por cada cabeza que tenga más allá de la primera. Incluso con un ataque fallido, la hidra inflige a la criatura objetivo el daño de un Golpe de colmillos, aunque falla por completo con un fallo crítico. Esto cuenta para el penalizador por ataques múltiples de la hidra como un número de ataques igual al número de cabezas que tenga.

action->Storm of Jaws.name: Tormenta de mandíbulas
action->Storm of Jaws.description: La hidra realiza un número de Golpes de hasta su número de cabezas, cada uno contra un objetivo diferente. Estos ataques cuentan para el penalizador por ataques múltiples de la hidra, pero el penalizador por ataques múltiples no aumenta hasta después de que la hidra haya realizado todos sus ataques.

Amelekana.name: Amelekana
Amelekana.publicNotes: Las amelekanas son depredadores anfibios de emboscada nativos de rios y lagos de Castrovel. Una amelekana se parece a un caracol gigante, con una concha espiral opalescente y un rostro sin ojos coronado por seis antenas, pero ahi terminan las semejanzas. En lugar de un unico pie enorme, posee tubos carnosos que se alzan por agujeros de la concha y multitud de patas pequenas y acorazadas, como las de un cangrejo. Sin embargo, se mueve con una rapidez sorprendente cuando detecta una presa.

action->Lifesense 100 pies.name:
<Compendium> la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.sebk9XseMCRkDqRg]
Lifesense 100 pies

action->Reflective Shell.name: Caparazón reflectante
action->Reflective Shell.description: Una amelekana sumergida en agua obtiene un bonificador por circunstancia +4 a las pruebas de Sigilo. Si el agua está en movimiento, este bonificador aumenta a +8.

action->Lob Amoeba.name: Lanzar ameba
action->Lob Amoeba.description:
La amelekana lanza una @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.gatewalkers-bestiary.Actor.HypIeplCDn0Phqs4]{Ameba simbiótica} contra un objetivo a 40 pies o menos. Es un ataque a distancia que no cuenta para el penalizador por ataques múltiples de la amelekana, y su penalizador por ataques múltiples no se aplica a este ataque.

Éxito El objetivo recibe @Damage[(2d4+8)[bludgeoning]] y la ameba simbiótica aterriza en una casilla adyacente al objetivo.

Fallo El objetivo no recibe daño, pero la ameba simbiótica aparece igualmente en una casilla adyacente al objetivo.

Fallo crítico El objetivo no recibe daño y la ameba lanzada muere con el impacto.

action->Symbiotic Amoeba.name: Ameba simbiótica
action->Symbiotic Amoeba.description:
Una ameba producida por la amelekana es una criatura Diminuta, sin mente y semiindependiente controlada por la amelekana. Tiene el rasgo esbirro, CA 15, 1 Punto de Golpe y las mismas habilidades y salvaciones que la amelekana. Cada asalto, la amelekana puede ordenar a un esbirro que haga que una ameba dé un Paso o Nade 20 pies y realice un Golpe de seudópodo (seudópodo cuerpo a cuerpo +13, daño 2d4 de ácido). Si una amelekana muere, sus amebas simbióticas también mueren por la reacción psíquica de la criatura anfitriona. Una amelekana puede tener hasta tres amebas simbióticas existentes al mismo tiempo.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.gatewalkers-bestiary.Actor.HypIeplCDn0Phqs4]{Ameba simbiótica}

Ancient Tupilaq.name: Tupilaq antiguo
Ancient Tupilaq.acDetails: (28 cuando está roto); armadura de constructo
Ancient Tupilaq.publicNotes: Un tupilaq es un constructo artisticamente tallado a partir de huesos de animales, normalmente de ballena o morsa, e imbuido con el proposito expreso de eviscerar a los enemigos de su creador. Surge de una magia cargada de odio, y solo puede crearlo alguien que crea haber sufrido una ofensa terrible. Cuando se comete un crimen imperdonable contra alguien con gran habilidad para tallar y conocimientos de magia, el deseo de venganza puede tomar forma en uno de estos constructos.

action->Construct Armadura (Hardness 11).name: Armadura de constructo (Dureza 11)
action->Construct Armadura (Hardness 11).description: Como los objetos normales, un tupilaq tiene Dureza. Esta Dureza reduce cualquier daño que reciba en una cantidad igual a la Dureza. Cuando un tupilaq queda reducido a menos de la mitad de sus Puntos de Golpe, o inmediatamente después de recibir daño de un impacto crítico, su armadura de constructo se rompe, pierde su Dureza y su CA se reduce a 28.

action->Carver's Curse.name: Maldición del tallador
action->Carver's Curse.description: Cuando se crea un tupilaq, la maldición impartida por su creador se manifiesta en forma de un único @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9AAkVUCwF6WVNNY2]{Rayo relampagueante} de rango 5 que el tupilaq puede lanzar tres veces al día. El conjuro concreto es un reflejo del deseo de venganza del creador.

Animate Dream.name: Sueño animado
Animate Dream.publicNotes: Un sueno animado se coagula a partir de siglos de fragmentos dispersos de ensonacion y sueno, dejados atras cuando las mentes dormidas derivan por la Dimension de los Suenos. En la mayoria de casos estos fragmentos se dispersan por si solos, pero cuando los sonadores huyen de pesadillas hacia el mundo despierto, pueden adquirir una vida sobrenatural propia. Tienen poco razonamiento o intencion mas alla de buscar fragmentos semejantes, absorberlos y crecer.

action->Endless Nightmare.name: Pesadilla interminable
action->Endless Nightmare.description:
El toque de un sueño animado llena la mente de la víctima con visiones aterradoras.

Salvación @Check[fortitude|dc:26]

Etapa 1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigado} (1 día)

Etapa 2 fatigado y @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Anonadado 1} (1 día)

Etapa 3 La víctima cae @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Inconsciente} y no puede ser despertada mientras permanezca en esta etapa (1 día).

Apothecary's Cabinet.name: Gabinete de boticario
Apothecary's Cabinet.acDetails: (20 cuando está roto); armadura de constructo

action->Construct Armadura (Hardness 10).name: Armadura de constructo (Dureza 10)
action->Construct Armadura (Hardness 10).description: Como los objetos normales, un gabinete de boticario tiene Dureza. Esta Dureza reduce cualquier daño que reciba en una cantidad igual a la Dureza. Cuando el gabinete de boticario queda reducido a menos de la mitad de sus Puntos de Golpe, o inmediatamente después de recibir daño de un impacto crítico, su armadura de constructo se rompe y su CA se reduce a 20.

action->Poison Stock.name: Surtido de venenos
action->Poison Stock.description:
Cuando el gabinete impacta a una criatura con su Golpe de botella de veneno, tira [[/br 1d4]] para determinar qué tipo de veneno salpica a la criatura golpeada:

  1. veneno nervioso (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Torpe 1})
  2. veneno debilitante (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Debilitado 1})
  3. veneno nauseabundo (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Indispuesto 1})
  4. veneno de mente nublada (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Anonadado 1}).

El objetivo debe intentar una salvación de @Check[fortitude|dc:24|traits:poison].

Éxito crítico La criatura no se ve afectada.

Éxito La criatura recibe @Damage[1d6[poison]].

Fallo La criatura recibe @Damage[2d6[poison]] y queda afectada por la condición asociada al veneno obtenido hasta el final de su siguiente turno.

Fallo crítico La criatura recibe @Damage[2d6[poison]] y queda afectada por la condición asociada al veneno obtenido durante [[/br 1d4+1 #Asaltos]] asaltos.

action->Alluring Spores.name: Esporas atrayentes
action->Alluring Spores.description:
Salvación @Check[fortitude|dc:19]

Duración máxima 6 asaltos

Etapa 1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinado} por la floración ártica (1 asalto)

Etapa 2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.9qGBRpbX9NEwtAAr]{Controlado} por la floración ártica (1 asalto)

action->Feed.name: Alimentarse
action->Feed.description: La floración ártica extrae nutrientes de una criatura viva que ha tragado y recupera @Damage[(3d8+24)[healing]] PG. La criatura tragada recibe @Damage[(2d12+8)[bludgeoning]] de daño.

action->Paralyzing Poison.name: Veneno paralizante
action->Paralyzing Poison.description:
Las plantas extienden brotes rastreros que desarrollan rápidamente bulbos púrpuras. Estos bulbos, los pólipos de la planta, hacen brotar muchas enredaderas largas y ganchudas antes de desprenderse de la planta madre. Las amapolas crepusculares viven poco, pero son activas y buscan alimento durante una semana aproximadamente antes de marchitarse y morir. Las amapolas no son peligrosas salvo que se las manipule, pues secretan un polvo fino que paraliza el sistema nervioso de las criaturas que entran en contacto con ellas.

Salvación @Check[fortitude|dc:19]

Duración máxima 6 asaltos

Etapa 1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Desprevenido} y @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Torpe 1} (1 asalto)

Etapa 2 desprevenido y @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Torpe 2} (1 asalto)

Etapa 3 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralizado} (1 asalto)

action->Pheromones.name: Feromonas
action->Pheromones.description: 5 miles. Arctic blooms communicate con others de su kind via airborne pheromones. They puede usar este form de communication a determine su relative distance a cada otro, call for help si ellos son under ataque o need sustenance, announce que ellos've detected prey, y convey similar basic concepts. Pheromones coat everything dentro de el aura y allow dusk poppies a perceive con su pheromones.

la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.uJSseLa57HZYSMUu]

Aspect of Ruun.name: Aspecto de Ruun
Aspect of Ruun.publicNotes: Los guias espirituales sabios estan entre los espiritus mas prudentes. A menudo adoptan formas de aves rapaces, como buhos, usando sus sentidos agudos para evaluar situaciones desde las alturas antes de descender en picado para ayudar a mortales en peligro. Los aventureros que se ganan la amistad de un guia sabio son afortunados: ademas de ofrecer consejo antes del conflicto, estos guias pueden restaurar y atender a sus aliados tras una disputa violenta.

conjuro->Truespeech (Constant).name:

Habla verdadera (constante)

action->Warning Hoot.name: Ulular de advertencia
action->Warning Hoot.description:
Desencadenante El búho de pecho pétreo está a punto de tirar una prueba de Percepción o Supervivencia para determinar la iniciativa

Efecto El búho de pecho pétreo lanza un ulular para advertir a sus aliados, concediendo a cada aliado un bonificador de circunstancia +1 a su tirada de iniciativa.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.RbyXD99lybxPK6yS]{Efecto: Ulular de advertencia}

action->Bond with Mortal.name: Vínculo con mortal
action->Bond with Mortal.description:
Frecuencia una vez al día

Efecto El guía espiritual forma un vínculo con una criatura mortal. Mientras existe el vínculo, los Puntos de Golpe actuales y máximos del guía espiritual aumentan en 14, el guía espiritual obtiene un bonificador de estado +2 a las tiradas de ataque y daño, y el guía espiritual y el mortal vinculado pueden comunicarse telepáticamente mientras estén en el mismo plano. El guía espiritual solo puede estar vinculado con un mortal a la vez, y puede volver a realizar esta acción para terminar el vínculo o formar uno nuevo (lo que también pone fin al anterior). El vínculo termina si el guía espiritual o el mortal mueren.

Este vínculo refuerza la conexión del guía espiritual con el Plano Material. Mientras está vinculado, el guía espiritual pierde los rasgos incorpóreo y espíritu, pierde sus inmunidades y resistencias, y sus Golpes pasan a infligir el daño físico apropiado (normalmente perforante o cortante) en lugar de daño de fuerza.

action->Bonded Strike.name: Golpe vinculado
action->Bonded Strike.description:
Requisitos El guía espiritual está actualmente Vinculado con un mortal

Efecto El guía espiritual realiza un Golpe de garra. Si este ataque impacta, el mortal vinculado puede gastar su reacción para Golpear al mismo objetivo.

action->Empowered Healing.name: Curación potenciada
action->Empowered Healing.description: Cuando el buho de pecho petreo lanza curar, tira d10 en lugar de d8.

Blackfrost Guecubu.name: Guecubu de escarcha negra
Blackfrost Guecubu.publicNotes:
A veces, un individuo comete actos de horror tan indescriptibles que la tierra que pisa queda marcada por su maldad. Con villanos así, ni siquiera matarlos y esparcir sus huesos basta para librar al mundo de su vil presencia. Sus almas vuelven a alzarse como guecubus, esqueletos horribles hechos de huesos chamuscados, carne podrida y tierra corrompida. Los guecubus recorren la tierra buscando a quienes consideran responsables de su muerte.

Un guecubu recuerda lo que le hicieron, y los recuerdos de la injusticia alimentan su odio incluso después de la muerte.

conjuro->Shape Stone (At Will).name:
<Compendium> la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.McnPlLFvKtQVXNcG]

Blackfrost Prophet.name: Profeta de escarcha negra
Blackfrost Prophet.publicNotes:
With their hulking physiques and the potent connection to the Crown of the World, saumen kar who succumb to blackfrost become especially dangerous blackfrost dead. Those who guarded the Temple of Aqakaru in life continue to do so in undeath, albeit even more vigilantly and much more violently. Blackfrost prophets, as these wardens are sometimes known, maintain their formidable intellect and innate connection to their boreal environment, though the curse of blackfrost has stripped them of their memories and filled their hearts with evil.

Estos shambling arctic horrors are dead in name alone. Las criaturas who succumb to the frigid elements while cursed by blackfrost don't become mere corpses entombed in ice but rather vicious undead capable of spreading the curse of blackfrost even further. Cracked, frostbitten flesh that emits a freezing vapor like steam; inexorable, unhindered strides through pies of ash-blackened snow; a vacant, icy-blue gaze devoid of humanity—the descriptions of blackfrost dead vary by the teller, but none can deny the supernatural dread these monsters evoke.

Blackfrost dead take a variety of forms. Most are mindless, lumbering brutes, largely indiscernible from mundane zombies except for the curse they can inflict. Others not only maintain their presence of mind but wield powers of psychic corruption not unlike those of blackfrost's originator, Osoyo, the Blackfrost Whale. What form a blackfrost dead takes depends primarily on the victim's psychic fortitude and its aptitude for occult magic.

Creating Blackfrost Dead

The simplest way to create a blackfrost dead is to use an existing undead, such as a zombie or a mummy, as tu base criatura. Replace the criatura's abilities with abilities from the list on this page. All blackfrost dead gain the cold rasgo and have at least one way to inflict blackfrost, often using one of their Golpes.

Curse of the Crown

Los muertos de escarcha negra solo se encuentran en torno a las Espiras Sin Nombre, under which a massive alien being named Osoyo remains imprisoned. Only recently has this ancient being stirred from its slumber, causing blackfrost to foam out of fissures in the ice and afflict unfortunate explorers. The spread of the blackfrost curse has been mercifully slow thus far, but with each criatura afflicted, Osoyo's reach expands ever outward.

Los grumetes de cabrestante son constructos disenados especificamente para la navegacion. Los capitanes que buscan lealtad y competencia inquebrantables podrian hacerlo mucho peor que contar con uno.

Construido para parecer y ocupar el lugar del cabrestante de un barco, el torno que sube y baja el ancla, un grumete de cabrestante es un cilindro rechoncho de madera envuelto en cuerda resistente. Tambien presenta pequenas clavijas en torno a su diametro, que puede usar para agarrar cabos del aparejo y ayudar a gobernar la nave.

Un grumete de cabrestante protege instintivamente el barco de su capitan. Con cuerdas cortas fijadas a sus lados puede azotar y derribar enemigos o realizar reparaciones de emergencia en si mismo o en la embarcacion. Mucho mas peligrosa es el ancla unida a su cuerda mas larga, que puede blandir en amplios arcos y recoger al instante.

Captain Salah.name: Capitán Salah
Captain Salah.publicNotes:
Centaurs are legendario hunters and trackers who resemble heavily muscled humans with the bodies of powerful horses from the waist down. They are typically reclusive but haughty, quick to assume that their handsome physiques and long history of cultural traditions make them superior to any two-legged folk they encounter. While stories of bloody clashes between centaurs and humanoid settlers are well known, centaurs are neither intrinsically bloodthirsty nor recklessly aggressive. Rather, they are proud and stubborn and do not take kindly to outsiders who encroach on their tierras ancestrales, some of which have been ruled by centaurs for thousands of years. Against despoilers of naturaleza who fail to heed their warnings, centaurs do not hesitate to use their finely honed hunting skills to inflict deadly wounds.

Centaurs train with armas as well as their heavy hooves, and the thunder of centaurs charging across the plains is often mistaken for a stampede or even an earthquake. Despite their insular naturaleza, some centaurs form close alliances with elves, fey, gnomes, and isolated human communities. Such aliados are often surprised to learn the depths of centaurs' honor, pragmatism, and wilderness LORE. Rarely, a centaur leaves its tribe to travel the wider world. Such lone centaur wanderers more easily integrate into humanoid societies, but other centaurs are quick to assume that some dishonor led to their exile and thus give such vagabonds a wide berth.

Centaurs have incredible variation in their individual size and coloration. Their upper bodies are fairly similar within a tribe and even region, but their lower bodies-like those of horses-can vary widely from parent to child. Most centaurs are at least 7 pies tall and weigh more than 2,000 pounds.

Centaurs live in groups of dozens of members, usually led by an old, powerful seer or battle-hardened warrior who has carried out many noble deeds and earned a lifetime of respect from their comrades. The revered leader guides the habits of their entire group; a wise seer might encourage the tribe to roam far from civilization to preserve the ways of its ancestors, while an aggressive warrior might foster skirmishes with nearby humanoid settlements and even rival centaur groups.

Creeping Evil.name: Mal reptante
Creeping Evil.publicNotes:
Religious philosophers have noted that while the virtuous are often filled with a righteous conviction that inures them from hopelessness and fear, the wicked are beset by constant doubt, driving them to commit even greater atrocities in an effort to stave off their insecurities. Sometimes, when this cycle reaches a crisis point, persistent doubt can even break from the psyche that created it, adopting a physical form known as a creeping evil.

While demons, devils, and other fiends are those most likely to spawn a creeping evil, a mortal tyrant gripped by constant fear of rebellion or a murderer compelled to kill again in order to cover up their previous crimes can manifest one as well. Often, a creeping evil will linger near the criatura that created it, sparing their life but lurking in the shadows as a constant reminder of their failures. Only when the criatura summons their courage and finally confronts their fear head-on does the creeping evil turn on them. Other creeping evils abandon their creators as soon as they spawn, slithering down lightless alleyways or into abandoned sewer tunnels to search for new souls to corrupt.

Though its body has the consistency of flowing tar, a creeping evil's predator-like cunning and unnatural ability to vary its volume at a whim set it apart from the living oozes often encountered by adventurers.

One criatura @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} by the creeping evil takes @Damage[4d8[mental]] daño (@Check[will|dc:28|basic] salvación). It can exit the container by taking this action again, immediately returning to its normal size. If criaturas or objects would occupy the creeping evil's space, it automatically pushes those criaturas and objects out of the way to fill a space.

Crownbound Constellation.name: Constelación vinculada a la corona
Crownbound Constellation.publicNotes:
Crownbound constellations are the essence of stars granted sentience by the goddess Desna, who created them to survey the vastness of space and help her craft the galaxy. Their intergalactic travels once took them far, but Lamashtu sought to ensnare Desna's creation. The Mother of Beasts lured them to Golarion and then, exploiting the power of Golarion's sun, corrupted their ability to star travel. Stranded on the planet and unable to bear sunlight, these criaturas traveled to the Crown of the World, where they have settled ever since.

An Eon's Long Memory

Crownbound constellations have not forgotten Lamashtu's DECEPTION, or the commission set for them by Desna. Crownbound constellations frequently attack those they assume to be in league with the Mother of Monsters, and their hatred for her has severed their connection to Desna, just as Lamashtu planned.

Demontangle.name: Demontangle
Demontangle.publicNotes:
Since the Worldwound opened over a century ago, countless demons have been slaughtered on the streets of Domora. Their remains sometimes coalesce into further unholy terrors, among the most gruesome examples of which are a trio of large, quivering tangles of knotted demon tongues. Estos “demontangles” haunt the city's streets day and night, slithering across the ruins in search of mortals to corrupt, destroy, and consume.

The tide washes ashore all manner of detritus, from harmless seaweed and shells to the rotting corpses of massive aquatic criaturas. The globster is often mistaken for such, and this assumption isn't entirely incorrect—these mindless, oozing masses are composed of decaying sea criaturas, half-digested and merged into a revolting, reeking heap of blubbery sludge.

Though mindless, globsters are predators that seek out living quarry. They often huddle on the seafloor, where their own fetid mass attracts scavengers who swiftly become the ooze's next meal. When the tides wash these monsters ashore, they simply shift to hunting land-bound prey. Coastal communities usually notice the smell of a washed-up globster long before they see it. Those sent to investigate often mistake a globster for the carcass of a beached whale before discovering the presumed corpse is very much alive and hungry.

Sages once believed globsters were undead, undulating wads of rotting flesh driven to feed, but though mindless, they are very much alive. They are attracted to waterside refuse dumps and floating garbage scows and are dimly aware enough to congregate where food is plentiful.

Since they consist of so much blubber and oily tissue, globsters can be collected for lamp oil, grease, cooking fat, and more. The goo that remains when they decompose works for this purpose, if one can stand the smell. The firmer fat deteriorates quickly, but many an impromptu goblin beach barbecue has deep-fried slabs of it as a delicacy.

Globsters consume living criaturas but digest only a portion of them. The undigested dross accumulates within the globster as it becomes more and more bloated. They carry this fetid mass within their squelching bodies until instinct or injury provokes them to vomit forth a new globster to help devour everything nearby. A globster with enough dross to create a new globster automatically does so as a free action triggered upon taking daño. Treat any encounter with such a globster as though it were against two nivel 5 criaturas, instead of just one. As far as scholars know, this is the only way these criaturas can create more of their kind.

Also known as "bubble cats" or "gas cats," desa-desas are small, vaguely feline predators that hunt the jungles of Castrovel. A typical desa-desa is roughly the size and shape of a bobcat. Its head is reptilian, sporting large eyes and slender fangs that protrude from its lips. Desa-desa fur tends to match their environment—most are dark green and brown—and is punctuated by patterns of small, bubble-like bladders that protrude from the criatura's skin like transparent boils. Every desa-desa has a different bladder pattern, and this distinctive anatomical feature is key to the criatura's SURVIVAL.

Desa-desas' lives giran alrededor de a little-understood (and likely magical) process by which the criaturas transform water into its constituent gaseous elements. A desa-desa stores these gasses in the polyp-like bladders, which are lined with an electricity-conducting material that allows the criatura to create sudden blasts of fame in all directions.

As a predator, the desa-desa's most dangerous attack is its bite, which passes along its bubble venom, which can ravage the fluids in the victim's own body. Este reaction causes water in el objetivo's cells to split rapidly, creating bubbles of gas that percolate through the criatura's flesh to its skin, where it balloons outward in large, agonizing blisters before popping. The combustible gasses in these blisters also make a criatura particularly susceptible to fire attacks—such as the desa-desa's defensive blast. A typical desa-desa is 4 pies long counting the tail, and weighs just 30 pounds.

Elder Thing.name: Elder Thing
Elder Thing.publicNotes:
The typical elder thing is a scientist first and anything else second, but they don't hesitate to use force to achieve their needs or defend their laboratories. When one does deign to speak to a non-elder thing, it's either out of fear (for a criatura they know vastly outstrips their own power) or with an insufferable sense of narcissistic superiority and impatience, like how an arrogant professor might speak to a student struggling with what they perceive to be a simple concept.

Known by various names on various worlds, but most often as "elder things" or "old ones," these alien criaturas are interested in creating lasting works of art, architecture, and even life (such as the legendario and dreaded shoggoth). Matched with their boundless capacity for egotism and enormous life spans, elder things often see themselves as the most learned and advanced species on any planet they visit, and tend to treat most other forms of life like a scientist might treat experimental stock. While not generally inimical or violent, their naturaleza often puts them at odds against other societies they encounter, and war is a time-honored solution. The elder things rarely shy away from using violence to secure their own territory and their perceived right to experiment and explore.

A typical elder thing is 6 pies tall from head to pies, with a 7-pies wingspan. Their bodies are radial in naturaleza, with five wings, five tentacle-like arms that each end in a writhing nest of tendrils, and five eyestalks. At one end of their barrel-shaped bodies are several larger tentacles they use for combat and locomotion, while at the other, at the center of their five eyes in their starfish-shaped heads, sits a single mouth rodeado by multicolored cilia. An elder thing's language is a mix of piping and whistling sounds, but they can vocalize a wide range of other languages as well—albeit with a strange, high-pitched accent.

Space Travelers

An elder thing can travel through outer space via flight, but it doesn't do so at a greater speed than its normal fly Velocidad. When an elder thing wishes to travel through the void of space, it typically aims itself in the direction it wishes to go, then enters a timed hibernation so that it wakes at a point where it nears its destination.

Glimmervine.name: Glimmervine
Glimmervine.publicNotes:
Glimmervines are carnivorous creeping vines with sparkling white flowers that open to bloom only at night. They flourish most in high altitudes and cold climates, where they survive by dazzling small prey with their iridescent blossoms before crushing them to death with impossibly strong tendrils. The blood and decomposing flesh of their prey seep into el suelo like fertilizer for glimmervines' roots to absorb as nutrients. Because scarps and gulleys caked with gore tend to deter future victims, glimmervines instinctively know not to linger in one spot for long.

Glimmervines are mostly dormant during the day. Clinging to the sides of mountains and cliffs, they're easily mistaken for mundane climbing plants such as ivy or morning glory. When night falls, though, glimmervines' spectacular reflective flowers make their entrancing naturaleza plain for all to see.

Glimmervines are closely related to assassin vines, who employ similar ambush tactics and feeding behaviors, but the former is easily discernible by the shiny white blooms in place of an assassin vine's small red berries. Estos petals are coated with iridescent veins that absorb sunlight during the day and give off an eerie yet beautiful glow at night. The glistening patina attracts pollinating insects.

On their own, glimmervines don't pose much of a threat to most criaturas. Though its root-based sensory organs are formidable in close proximity, a glimmervine can't sense criaturas farther than 60 pies away, making escape as easy as getting out of range of their slow movement. The true danger of these plants comes from glimmervine thickets—dense patches of glimmervines that can entangle entire hillsides or ravines. Woe be unto a hapless traveler caught in the midst of a glimmervine thicket at sundown.

Gokeki.name: Gokeki
Gokeki.publicNotes:
A gokeki looks like a cross between a monkey and a scorpion, with a harpoon of solidified webbing connected to spinnerets at its aft end, held by the coiled, scorpion-like tail that acts like an atlatl. Adding further to the gokeki's bizarre appearance are the criatura's extra pair of eyes and the nearly vestigial pincers sprouting from its chest. Gokeki fur is generally light tan in color, darkening noticeably toward the criatura's tail, although subspecies with bright green, yellow, or even fluorescent pink or purple fur have also been reported.

Unlike many of Castrovel's native criaturas, gokekis aren't generally regarded to be a product of natural evolution, but rather the result of a genetic experiment that broke loose from its creator and escaped into the wild. Gokekis have adapted frighteningly well to the planet's harsh jungle environment, although thankfully they seem to lack both the INTELLIGENCE and sociability often exhibited by primates. Gokekis hunt alone or, more rarely, in mated pairs. Attempts to domesticate gokekis often result in the death of their would-be owners, although when provided with a proper range in which to hunt, gokekis can serve as guardians for those looking to deter unwanted visitors.

Though dangerous predators, gokekis are highly sought after by Castrovel's hunting cultures, particularly the lizardfolk and tripkees who call the jungle continent of Ukulam their home. The former value gokekis for their webbing harpoons, which function as ready-made javelins. Meanwhile, tripkees harvest the gokeki's filament gland to aid in the construction of the treetop homes. Both peoples also eat gokeki meat, which when properly prepared can be made into a flavorful and hearty jerky.

Harvested Treasures

While gokekis aren't intelligent enough to gather treasure of their own, many natives of Castrovel consider their bodies a valuable resource. If harvested with a successful @Check[nature|dc:17] or @Check[survival|dc:17] prueba, the gokeki's filament gland can be used as 25 gp worth of raw materials for potent glues such as @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.7IrQPyMm76nLVoXx]{Everlasting Adhesive}. The filament itself is identical to a 60-pies length of rope. Finally, the criatura's harpoon can be used as a javelin.

The tree fisher can move while it has a criatura grabbed with its filament, but automatically releases the GRAB if the tree fisher moves beyond the filament's 60-pies length. A criatura grabbed by the filament at the beginning of its turn takes @Damage[5[bleed]].

The tree fisher can sever the filament and release any criatura grabbed by it as a free action. The filament can be severed by a Golpe that deals at least @Damage[10[slashing]] to it. Este doesn't deal any daño to the tree fisher itself. The filament has AC 17, and its @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SkZAQRkLLkmBQNB9]{Escape} DC is 19.

The tree fisher has only one harpoon; if the filament is severed, the tree fisher loses this ability and its ranged attack for 1 week as it fashions a new harpoon.

Green Monkey.name: Mono verde
Green Monkey.publicNotes:
Nimble spirit guides are small and discreet, using their diminutive size and natural agility to dart from hiding place to hiding place. They tend to be much shyer than other spirit guides, at least initially, preferring to watch nearby mortals from a distance before deciding whether to trust them. When their trust is so earned, nimble spirit guides are often playful and contagiously exuberant. Estos spirit guides can often be found entertaining lost children with antics until they are rescued or freeing prisoners by stealing keys and picking locks.

The green monkey is a nimble spirit guide who takes the appearance of a tiny primate with green fur that, on closer inspection, turns out to be fine blades of grass.

Spirit guides are ghostly criaturas that manifest as primordial animals in the Universe. Many Sarkorian cultures believe that spirit guides came into being as the first mortal hunting bands began to form. In this time before time, spirit guides adopted the most elemental shapes of animals, and they taught humanoid communities about important aspects of naturaleza, such as where to find fresh water, which plants were safe to eat, and how to live in harmony with their environment. As they imparted their wisdom, spirit guides took more physical forms, eventually becoming the wild animals that exist today. Though spirit guides bestowed most of their gifts unto mortals in ancient times, a rare few continue to lurk in forgotten or as-of-yet-undiscovered corners of the physical world.

Spirit Guide Companions

One way to gain the aid of a spirit guide is to take the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.vx5FGEG34AxI2dow.JournalEntryPage.J0AfK0jJgS5WxhCE]{scion of Domora} archetype. Este archetype allows character to elige a spirit guide to accompany them on their adventures—provided they first prove themselves worthy of the honor.

The Sarkoris Scar

Some spirit guides encountered in the haunted badlands now known as the Sarkoris Scar are remnants of god calling, an ancient tradition practiced by many Sarkorian cultures. Severed from their callers by the demonic war that devastated the land for over a century, such gods now roam the blasted landscape, occasionally helping those they find worthy.

Immolis.name: Immolis
Immolis.publicNotes:
Most complex organisms, whether plant or animal, produce energy by converting fuel (such as food) into heat. Though this process is invaluable, it's also a vulnerability—one that the immolis has evolved to exploit.

Immolises are psychic predators found all across Castrovel, especially bajo tierra and in cool environs. Mostly blind, they hunt by sensing the body heat of other criaturas. When an immolis acquires a objetivo, it focuses its innate psychic energies in an invisible beam aimed at its prey. The sudden influx of energy causes el objetivo's metabolism to accelerate rapidly, spurring the criatura's body to produce energy at a dangerous rate. Este sudden rush of heat literally cooks the criatura internally—innards burst, blood boils, and fat catches fire. The end result isn't just warm food, but a meal roasted to morbid perfection.

An immolis's basic shape resembles that of a spidery, spindly frog covered in delicate scales. The head has a simian muzzle, the lips of which pull back to reveal a squid-like beak. Above the mouth, the criatura has three pairs of nostrils, which fare and chuff as the criatura hunts. Though they walk with a hunch, immolises CLIMB with shocking speed.

Unlike many other pyro-predators, immolises have a deep and paradoxical fear of fire, perhaps because they know how easily any flesh—their own included—can blacken and burn. As a result, they prefer to lair near water. Este presents its own problem, however, as their heat sense is easily disrupted by criaturas taking steps to hide their heat signatures, such as submerging themselves in water or snow. While intelligent enough to communicate and band together with others of their kind, immolises view all other species as either prey or threats and have as little interest in cultural exchange as in personal possessions. The average immolis stands 5 pies tall and weighs 150 pounds.

Kareq.name: Kareq
Kareq.publicNotes:
A kareq looks like a cross between a dinosaur and an insect. The kareq's torso extends back into a bulbous abdomen like an ant's.

A kareq has a resonance chamber in its lower body, and when it flexes its muscular back legs against it, pressure builds up and sound waves are amplified and then focused as the kareq opens its mouth and releases the blast. The resulting shock wave can easily kill.

Kareqs are thought to be related to Golarion's destrachans, though their similarities may simply be the result of convergent evolution. Unlike the stronger subterranean destrachans, kareqs are native to a variety of different environments, most often jungles and forests. A few sandy-colored species are found in the deserts of the Colonies, where formians regard the beasts as noble or, in some cases, practically sacred.

Kareqs tend to be solitary predators, bold and unafraid, even willing to take on predators significantly larger than themselves. In combat, they keep their distance at first, softening up opponents with their boomstrikes before moving in for the kill with their claws.

While they don't usually hunt in populated areas, kareqs are extremely territorial, and their desire to lay claim to tall landscape features can bring them into conflict with humanoids. During mating season, a kareq seeks height, climbing to the top of hills, boulders, or—if a settlement is particularly unlucky—towers and other buildings. From these perches, kareqs blast out their booming mating call which can carry for dozens of miles.

A typical kareq stands 5 pies tall at the shoulder and is 10 pies long, weighing up to 300 pounds.

Kvernknurr.publicNotes:
Kvernknurrs are lanky fey giants that dwell in cold-water rivers and lakes. A kvernknurr's blue flesh allows it to camoufage itself in its preferred environ, where it haunts local millers and farmers by sabotaging water wheels and farm equipment.

A kvernknurr's most distinguishing feature is its oversized mouth and the two rows of axe-like teeth therein. To eat, a kvernknurr need only unhinge its lower jaw, revealing in the process a yawning portal nearly the size of a human doorway—convenient, considering its favorite food is humans and their ilk.

A lake- or riverbed is the perfect place for a kvernknurr to sleep off a big meal. It's also a perilous circumstance for swallowed prey lucky enough to escape the kvernknurr's belly. "Out of the belly, into the water," goes one lakeside village saying.

Kverknurrs despise humanoid-made disturbances to the waters in which they live, even seemingly harmless ones like waterwheels. In their anger, kvernknurrs use their oversized jaws to clamp down on such machinery. When townsfolk come to investigate their jammed mill, the kvernknurr then springs out from hiding to attack, roaring terribly before snatching a victim to eat whole. Folks brave enough to attack a kvernknurr soon learn to fight up close; the wily monster is quick enough to snatch arrows and spears in its jaws midair before swallowing the armas down.

Leiko.publicNotes:
Shae are wispy, tenebrous criaturas native to the Plane of Shadow. Their amorphous bodies appear in constant states of flux. They cast no shadows of their own, instead gaining and losing umbral energy to nearby shadows that shrink and grow alongside them.

Most shae wear clothing spun from shadows that shift with them, though diplomats sometimes don more conventional garments while entertaining outsiders. Their most distinctive apparel are their white stone masks, which shae don only when they must put on a discernible "face" for interacting with humanoids and similar criaturas. They do so begrudgingly, as they consider themselves superior to humanoids, but donning their masks allows them to be more easily understood and thus keeps their interactions with their lessers as brief as possible.

The dynamic between a shae and humanoids shifts when humanoids come to worship a shae, however. A mortal who shows a shae their due deference is digno de tener cerca, so many shae collect cults of personality or expansive entourages. Even getting a meeting with such a self-important shae can present a challenge that requires one to deal with many layers of hangers-on who insist on vetting the newcomer before wasting the shae's precious time.

According to shae LORE, they've transcended the material world and now embody a cosmological equilibrium of reality and illusion. Their claims to metaphysical ascendance and knowledge of the secrets of shadows entice many mortal supplicants to join shae courts and cults. In the shae language, their name means "unbound," in accordance with their belief that their ephemeral naturaleza makes them free of the moral and social strictures that bind other sentient criaturas, and they essentially make a virtue of capriciousness. Shae feel little obligation to follow through with oaths or obey laws, so sealing a compact with a mortal means little to them.

Mindmoppets are willing servants to anyone who concerns themselves with strenuous mental exercise. Their creator is usually an obvious first choice, and they serve them dutifully. However, they have only an academic understanding of good and evil, of ethics, or mortal limitations. They see service to their maestro's science as the ultimate standard by which they judge their actions or those of others. Mindmoppets appear to have some ability to see a short distance into the future, though this might only be that their innate interest for thought and cognition gives them a knack for anticipating the actions of others.

Ocluai.languages: no puede hablar ningún idioma; telepathy 100 pies, images only
Ocluai.publicNotes:
Ocluais embody the fear of being lost and helpless in the darkness as well as the danger of unreasoning terror. An ocluai's gray body resembles that of a featherless owl with a serrated beak, the legs of a monkey, and oversized eye sockets full of shadow. The field of unnatural darkness that rodea an ocluai disorients most criaturas; while other gorgas are quick to move in for the kill, ocluais love to perch on a low branch or lintel and watch with their blank expressions as prey succumbs to panic. Though capable fighters, ocluais prefer to hang back and slash at those whose frantic flight brings them within range, letting their prey's own terror drive them over cliffs or bring them to their knees.

Ocluais understand several languages but rarely communicate with non-fey. When they do, their communication takes the form of unsettling telepathic images projected directly into the other party's mind as the ocluai holds their gaze.

Gorgas are fey embodiments of diurnal criaturas' fear of the dark. Beings of shadow and hunger, they love to prey upon light-loving criaturas. Many different kinds of gorgas exist, and each embodies a different facet of the night's countless terrors.

Gorgas are common in the First World realm of Nighthold, where they once served the mysterious Count Ranalc. After Ranalc's disappearance, the gorgas quickly lost what little compassion they had, scattered into small bands led by their strongest members, and began hunting any fey they could find. All gorgas carry shrouds of shadow within them, and most find daylight unpleasant, tending to remain within Nighthold's perpetual gloom or hole up in caverns or deep forests until night falls. Their bizarre eyes—hollow pools of magical shadow—allow them to see even in magical darkness.

Gorgas and Elves

For thousands of years, gorgas have sought vengeance for the loss of their beloved Count Ranalc. A few centuries ago, a fey schemer named Kaneepo the Slim saw in the shadowy criaturas' grudge an opportunity to carry out their own vendetta. The slick-tongued fey convinced a group of gorgas that elves were behind Count Ranalc's disappearance and that the gorgas could achieve vengeance if they joined Kaneepo's assaults on the Universe. Though some of the brighter gorgas have seen through the ruse, most are content to have an outlet for their fury.

Other Gorgas

As many different types of gorgas exist as there are ways to fear the dark. The fear of losing one's sole source of illumination—a flickering torch in a rainstorm, the last candle on a moonless night—manifests as a notua, capable of snuffing lights as well as lives. When the dark makes distant objects appear to be something other than they are—a tree trunk seems to be a crouching beast, a drape of moss becoming a dangling snake—the gaiomyr gorga dances with delight and brings its victims' imagined dangers to horrific life. Some gorgas, it's said, represent nocturnal fears that defy description altogether—the fear of unknown unknowns, perhaps.

Ogmunzorius.name: Ogmunzorius
Ogmunzorius.publicNotes:
An animate dream coalesces from centuries of stray fragments of reverie and dream left behind as slumbering minds drift through the Dimension of Dreams. In most cases, these fragments simply disperse on their own, but when dreamers flee from nightmares back to the waking world, these fragments can take on a supernatural life of their own. They have little reasoning and intent except to seek similar fragments, absorb them, and grow. When enough of them gather together, they merge into a horrific form as an animate dream.

Individually, animate dreams can hold a wide range of appearances, but most take on rudimentary shapes akin to the living forms of the minds that spawned them. Animate dreams that rise from slumbering humanoids, the most commonly encountered, thus appear humanoid, but with distorted, nightmarish shapes that incorporate additional twisted limbs and frightening features. In these forms, animate dreams find their way out of the Dreamlands and into the waking world, only to discover they have no way of returning and suffer a relentless hunger that only new nightmares can sate.

An animate dream thrives on the terror fueled by nightmares and fear and uses its supernatural abilities to invoke such feelings in the minds of its victims, cursing its prey by creating a permanent link to that individual's dreams. Thereafter, the victim is subjected to all manner of reoccurring nightmares. As the nightmares continue, the victim finds it more and more difficult to remain awake. In the end, the victim plunges into an accursed slumber from which it cannot return. Estos victims provide the animate dream with the purest form of fear and are its preferred sustenance.

An animate dream can subsist on the ambient fear generated by regular nightmares, but these lesser fears aren't as satisfying, often driving the animate dream to seek out new victims. Left without a source of fear, an animate dream won't starve to death, but it will grow increasingly violent and desperate. Famished animate dreams are the ones most often encountered, as they have been forced to abandon subtlety to pursue more blatant methods of harvesting fear. Yet such animate dreams also tend to be the least powerful of their kind. Those who have grown metaphysically fat on fear have generally done so by adopting a specific nightmare theme, such as being buried alive, being swept away by ocean waves, or being consumed by wild beasts. Such animate dreams often have similarly themed innate conjuros to augment their powers.

Some maintain that these wasps are manifestations of Calistria's vengeance, but her faithful believe something closer to the truth—that these wasps represent a mockery of vengeance and a corruption of the directed rage their goddess teaches and epitomizes. Skin Beetle.name: Escarabajo de piel
Skin Beetle.publicNotes:
A typical skin beetle is 1-1/2 pies long and weighs 10 pounds—about the size of a house cat. Its oval-shaped body is covered in dull-colored scales, and short, club-like antennae stem from shallow grooves in its head.

Skin beetles are found in most environments that can sustain life, from cold, dry steppes to dense, humid jungles. They use their complex multi-jointed mandibles to strip the skin and flesh from recently deceased criaturas with almost surgical precision. While skin beetles eat most of what they remove, they also preserve chunks for later by coating it in special salivary secretions similar to formaldehyde. The skin beetle rolls this coated flesh into a ball, then stores it under an exposed tree root or rock for leaner times. Signs of skin beetle activity include excoriated skeletons and the smell of the beetles' preservative saliva.

Umasi Beetle Masters

Though best known for flaying carrion, skin beetles can also heal gravely wounded individuals. Skin beetles can graft preserved flesh onto a dying animal or humanoid. The end result isn't pretty, but it sometimes works. From the perspective of the healed, the blessing can be mixed, as the beetle's surgery often transforms the subject into a patchwork aberration called an @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-bestiary-3.Actor.mupW1Mgec250lQiZ]{Umasi}.

Umasi created by skin beetles sometimes develop supernatural connections to their insectoid saviors. Such umasi can command skin beetles to harvest more flesh to keep their decaying bodies intact.

Stone-Breasted Owl.name: Búho de pecho pétreo
Stone-Breasted Owl.publicNotes:
Sage spirit guides are among the wisest spirits. They often take the forms of raptors such as owls, using their keen senses to evaluate situations from high above before swooping in to aid imperiled mortals.

Adventurers who befriend a sage guide are fortunate indeed; in addition to providing sage counsel before conflict begins, sage guides can restore and tend to their aliados in the aftermath of a violent dispute.

In many stories, the sage guide assumes the form of a large owl whose proud breast is composed of hard stone. Este depiction combines the wisdom commonly attributed to the owl with the strength and fortitude of the earth.

Spirit guides are ghostly criaturas that manifest as primordial animals in the Universe. Many Sarkorian cultures believe that spirit guides came into being as the first mortal hunting bands began to form. In this time before time, spirit guides adopted the most elemental shapes of animals, and they taught humanoid communities about important aspects of naturaleza, such as where to find fresh water, which plants were safe to eat, and how to live in harmony with their environment. As they imparted their wisdom, spirit guides took more physical forms, eventually becoming the wild animals that exist today. Though spirit guides bestowed most of their gifts unto mortals in ancient times, a rare few continue to lurk in forgotten or as-of-yet-undiscovered corners of the physical world.

Spirit Guide Companions

One way to gain the aid of a spirit guide is to take the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.vx5FGEG34AxI2dow.JournalEntryPage.J0AfK0jJgS5WxhCE]{scion of Domora} archetype. Este archetype allows character to elige a spirit guide to accompany them on their adventures—provided they first prove themselves worthy of the honor.

The Sarkoris Scar

Some spirit guides encountered in the haunted badlands now known as the Sarkoris Scar are remnants of god calling, an ancient tradition practiced by many Sarkorian cultures. Severed from their callers by the demonic war that devastated the land for over a century, such gods now roam the blasted landscape, occasionally helping those they find worthy.

Temagyr.name: Temagyr
Temagyr.publicNotes:
Temagyrs embody the fear of nocturnal hunters—predators that stalk through the dark of night and attack when their prey is most vulnerable. Able to blend in with and step between shadows to surprise victims, temagyrs delight in ambush tactics.

An average temagyr is 8 pies long and weighs 500 pounds but moves with unnatural fluidity and grace, the shadows they carry seeming to hang in the air behind them. In combat, a temagyr can take down opponents either with physical attacks or by taking bites out of their enemigo's shadow. Estos shadow wounds, which remain visible unless healed, often perplex doctors and investigators from the Universe; a corpse from a temagyr attack can appear pristine, its tattered shadow the only clue to how it met its untimely fate.

Gorgas are fey embodiments of diurnal criaturas' fear of the dark. Beings of shadow and hunger, they love to prey upon light-loving criaturas. Many different kinds of gorgas exist, and each embodies a different facet of the night's countless terrors.

Gorgas are common in the First World realm of Nighthold, where they once served the mysterious Count Ranalc. After Ranalc's disappearance, the gorgas quickly lost what little compassion they had, scattered into small bands led by their strongest members, and began hunting any fey they could find. All gorgas carry shrouds of shadow within them, and most find daylight unpleasant, tending to remain within Nighthold's perpetual gloom or hole up in caverns or deep forests until night falls. Their bizarre eyes—hollow pools of magical shadow—allow them to see even in magical darkness.

Gorgas and Elves

For thousands of years, gorgas have sought vengeance for the loss of their beloved Count Ranalc. A few centuries ago, a fey schemer named Kaneepo the Slim saw in the shadowy criaturas' grudge an opportunity to carry out their own vendetta. The slick-tongued fey convinced a group of gorgas that elves were behind Count Ranalc's disappearance and that the gorgas could achieve vengeance if they joined Kaneepo's assaults on the Universe. Though some of the brighter gorgas have seen through the ruse, most are content to have an outlet for their fury.

Other Gorgas

As many different types of gorgas exist as there are ways to fear the dark. The fear of losing one's sole source of illumination—a flickering torch in a rainstorm, the last candle on a moonless night—manifests as a notua, capable of snuffing lights as well as lives. When the dark makes distant objects appear to be something other than they are—a tree trunk seems to be a crouching beast, a drape of moss becoming a dangling snake—the gaiomyr gorga dances with delight and brings its victims' imagined dangers to horrific life. Some gorgas, it's said, represent nocturnal fears that defy description altogether—the fear of unknown unknowns, perhaps.

Tales tell of strange humanoids who harvest appendages and organs from other criaturas to graft onto their own perpetually decaying bodies. Estos stories are encountered more often than their subject, however. A reclusive people, umasi live deep in remote jungles, largely isolated from other societies.

Despite not being undead, umasi can't heal naturally or via magic. Instead, they must harvest appendages and organs from the living to perpetuate their own lives. Estos modifications require special techniques, obscure rituals, and often the assistance of other umasi. Shorter rituals make quick repairs to wounded flesh-even consuming a nutrient-rich organ of a recently slain criatura can provide quick rejuvenation-while more extensive changes require a full day's work.

Because of the naturaleza of their existences, no one single form remains common to umasi. Many graft any number of arms or legs of various sizes on their bodies, while others are conglomerations of exotic beasts, other humanoids, and whatever criaturas they've hunted or scavenged. However, all umasi remain vaguely humanoid in shape. An umasi with additional arms can hold or wield more items at once, while additional legs or other limbs might grant increased Velocidad or new types of Velocidad. Concepts such as gender, ethnicity, and even recognizing someone based on their appearance are irrelevant to umasi. Instead, they value age and experience and identify themselves with iconic adornments or speech patterns.

Despite their morbid naturaleza, umasi are rarely at odds with living criaturas. Estos opportunistic hunters value their self-preservation, but use fast-acting nonlethal poisons to subdue their objetivos for safe and minimally destructive harvesting. Few umasi harbor malice toward the living, but some possess a streak of self-loathing and search for powerful magics that might break whatever curse binds them to their current state. Rarely, an umasi finds some strange form of acceptance on the fringes of a remote community where their skills at MEDICINE carry more weight than fear of their strange appearances.

Yaiafineti.name: Yaiafineti
Yaiafineti.publicNotes:
Yaiafinetis grow only during periods of extended twilight, thriving across the cold tundra of the Crown of the World exclusively in the winter months. To survive in such harsh conditions, the yaiafineti, or dusk poppy, sprouts independent polyps that detach and then creep across the tundra in search of food for their matriarch.

Dusk poppies sprout from spores that attach to carcasses, but they only blossom during the long twilight unique to the Crown of the World. The perfect conditions for their development are so rare that yaiafineti have developed a vigorous appetite. They feed unceasingly. Much of their energy goes to developing more polyps, and one plant can easily spawn a small infestation of these deadly bulbs.

The plants send out runner shoots that quickly develop purple bulbs. Estos bulbs, the plant's polyps, sprout many long, hooked vines before detaching from the mother plant. Polyps are short lived but active, foraging for a week or so before they shrivel and die. Estos polyps aren't dangerous unless handled. They secrete a fine dust that acts as a paralyzing poison that seizes the nervous system of criaturas who come in contact with them.

Violet Dusk Poppy dye

Some natives of the Crown of the World hunt yaiafineti matriarchs and harvest their petals, which are used to create an expensive, glimmering violet dye. Although the polyps are far less useful for this purpose, skilled trackers follow their vine tracks back to their matriarch.

The plants send out runner shoots that quickly develop purple bulbs. Estos bulbs, the plant's polyps, sprout many long, hooked vines before detaching from the mother plant. Polyps are short lived but active, foraging for a week or so before they shrivel and die. Estos polyps aren't dangerous unless handled. They secrete a fine dust that acts as a paralyzing poison that seizes the nervous system of criaturas who come in contact with them.
